topics.topic: Portal handling of identical PhotoPublication replay while the existing photo is hidden
questions: What does the Portal do when the calling flow submits an identical PhotoPublication again while the first Portal photo remains hidden?
What does the Portal do when the same PhotoPublication body is sent again while the existing photo remains hidden?

Is the Portal required to return the existing photo when an identical publication body is sent again while that photo is hidden, or is the result left to the Portal? This claim needs an owner decision or must remain an open question under R0-04.

quotes:
- Continuity: It is not changed after it is built. The same body sent again gets the same photo from
  the Portal while the photo is hidden.
judgement.why: The text explicitly requires the Portal to return the same hidden photo when the same publication body is sent again.

topics.topic: PublicationMark duplicate recording behavior and timestamp preservation
questions: When record-publication is called again with the same photo_id, must it return the original mark with status replayed, or may it refuse the duplicate or replace its timestamp?
When the same photo_id is recorded again for an existing placement, must the deliverer return the original mark with its original marked_at, or may it reject or rewrite the mark?

When the same photo_id is recorded again for an existing placement, must the deliverer return the original mark with its original marked_at, reject the duplicate, or replace its timestamp? This claim needs an owner decision or must remain an open question under R0-04.

quotes:
The record that a placed photo became one Portal photo (R0-08). The calling flow reports the
`photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark. The scan and a
repeated placement read it, so a flow does not publish the photo again. The same `photo_id` again
returns the first mark; another `photo_id` is refused.

**Enumeration:** `MarkStatus` is `marked` for the call that created the mark and `replayed` for a
later call with the same `photo_id`. It is part of the answer to that call and is not stored.
- Continuity: The first mark stands when it is sent again, and its `marked_at` does not change.
judgement.why: The text requires a duplicate with the same photo_id to return the first mark with replayed status and its original marked_at.

topics.topic: Repeated PhotoPlacement delivery after its source file is removed
questions: When a placement exists but its source file is no longer in the folder, does a repeated delivery return the stored placement or refuse the request because the source cannot be read?
After a placement exists and its source file leaves the folder, does another delivery request return the stored placement or fail because the source is unavailable?

After a placement exists and its source file leaves the folder, must a repeated delivery request return the stored placement, or must it fail because the source is unavailable? This claim needs an owner decision or must remain an open question under R0-04.

quotes:
The record that one source photo of one project was placed in the Portal binary store. The
deliverer creates it once when placing a photo. A repeated placement returns it and writes nothing
(P-06).
- Continuity: The same placement is returned after the source file has left the folder.
judgement.why: The text expressly says that repetition returns the existing placement without writing even after the source file has left the folder.

topics.topic: ServiceExit ownership, closed members, meanings, and process exit mappings
questions: What is the closed set of ServiceExit outcomes, and is ServiceExit a State 1 enum or a contract-only model introduced by A8?
What is the closed set of ServiceExit members, what does each member mean, and which process exit status does each choose?
What is the closed set of ServiceExit members and what process outcome does each member represent before the model closure is handed to later states?

quotes:
`ServiceExit` is the way the service process ends, which chooses its exit status; it is an enumeration of the
process, not a model of this state. A8 decides its outcomes, and the State 6 model closure gives its members.

`EXIT_STATUSES` holds exactly one row for each member of = models.ServiceExit, keyed by `outcome`; a
member without its row stops the build. = models.ServiceExit is START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the
process ends before its web server listens, whatever ends it; SERVED, value `served`: after it listens, a
signal of the imported `STOP_SIGNALS` constant stops it and the process ends without a failure; and
SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it listens, the process ends in any other way.

| `outcome` | `status` |
|---|---|
| `START_FAILED` | 1 |
| `SERVED` | 0 |
| `SERVER_FAILED` | 1 |
judgement.why: State 1 classifies ServiceExit as a process enumeration outside its model closure, while the later rules close its three members, meanings, serialized values, and exit-status mappings.
